v01-compartir-cadaques.name: Compartir Cadaqués
v01-compartir-cadaques.neighborhood: Old town, Riera de Sant Vicenç (the dry riverbed running down to the bay)
tags: Essential, book days/weeks ahead online or by phone; whole-table tasting served to all diners
v01-compartir-cadaques.why: Opened 2012 by Mateu Casañas, Oriol Castro and Eduard Xatruch — the trio whose Disfrutar (Barcelona) took a third Michelin star and World's 50 Best No.1 in 2024; Michelin Guide listed, two Soles Repsol To order: The whole-table tasting menu anchored by an Empordà seafood rice; the gazpacho-and-pesto starter is the house signature carried from elBulli days Seasonal — closes in deep winter; this is elBulli-trained refinement, not a casual harbourside lunch. Confirm opening dates before a winter trip.
v01-compartir-cadaques.address: Riera de Sant Vicenç s/n, 17488 Cadaqués, Girona
v01-compartir-cadaques.verdict: elBulli-trained refinement on the harbour — book it for the rice, not for a casual lunch.
v01-compartir-cadaques.signature: The whole-table tasting menu, anchored by an Empordà seafood rice.
v01-compartir-cadaques.person: The Disfrutar trio — Casañas, Castro & Xatruch; elBulli alumni.

signal_chip.label: Michelin
signal_chip.cosign: the elBulli line on the water — the one we'd book first

v01-compartir-cadaques.caveat: Seasonal — closes in deep winter; confirm dates before a winter trip.
v01-compartir-cadaques._lane: The elBulli line and the sea wall

v05-talla.name: Talla
v05-talla.neighborhood: West side of the harbour, Riba Pitxot (water's edge, looking back at the white town)
tags: Book ahead — reliably full; reservations online or by phone
v05-talla.why: Waterfront kitchen pairing traditional Catalan base with avant-garde technique; runs an adjoining Oli Bar; consistently top-ranked among Cadaqués tables To order: Flame-grilled oysters with ponzu, or the seaweed salad with goose barnacles (percebes) and razor clams Closed roughly November to March. Small terrace, books out fast in July-August.
v05-talla._lane: The elBulli line and the sea wall

v04-es-baluard.name: Es Baluard
v04-es-baluard.neighborhood: Waterfront, built into the old-town sea wall on Riba Nemesi Llorens
tags: Recommended in season; book by phone
Lunch on the first-floor terrace over the bay
v04-es-baluard.why: Opened 1967 by Quimet Seriñana and Maria Torrents; now third-generation, run by son Josep Seriñana with Fanni Puig and children Aina and Adrià To order: Monkfish (rap) suquet — the slow-simmered Empordà fish-and-potato stew the house is known for High-season opening only — largely shut outside summer. Built into the literal sea wall; book the window tables.
v04-es-baluard.hours: Lunch on the first-floor terrace over the bay
v04-es-baluard._lane: The elBulli line and the sea wall

v02-casa-anita.name: Casa Anita
v02-casa-anita.neighborhood: Old town, Carrer Miquel Rosset (uphill from the waterfront, near the church)
tags: No printed menu and no normal booking — it is a 'sung' menu recited at communal tables; turn up and wait
v02-casa-anita.why: Open since the 1960s; a Dalí haunt run by the Mota family — founder Ana Mota's death was reported by Catalan press as the loss of a village institution To order: House-salted Cadaqués anchovies and grilled Roses prawns, then the ice cream churned on site Cash culture, shared tables, no à la carte card — the order is recited aloud. Idiosyncratic by design.
v02-casa-anita.verdict: The village institution Dalí drank at — you order what they recite, not what you planned.
v02-casa-anita.signature: House-salted Cadaqués anchovies, grilled Roses prawns, then the ice cream churned on site.
v02-casa-anita.person: Run by the Mota family since the 1960s — founder Ana Mota.
v02-casa-anita.caveat: Cash only, shared tables, no menu card — the order is recited aloud.

v06-can-rafa.name: Can Rafa
v06-can-rafa.why: Family-run since 1982 by the Martín Faixó family; proximity cooking off the Cadaqués fishing boats and Cap de Creus dives To order: Arròs de bogavante (lobster rice) or langostino rice, sized for sharing; desserts handmade by Carmen Rice and fideuà are made for two-plus — don't order solo. Phone not independently verified.

v08-casa-nun.name: Casa Nun
v08-casa-nun.neighborhood: Old town, Plaça des Portitxó (small square just up from the bay)
v08-casa-nun.why: Over 40 years on the same square; the gratinated sardine is a house recipe carried across generations To order: Arròs caldós de bogavante (soupy lobster rice) — repeatedly called the best in town — and the sardina gratinada Family-run and small; phone not independently verified — walk in or use a booking platform.

v07-la-sirena.name: La Sirena
v07-la-sirena.neighborhood: Old town, Carrer d'es Call (one block up from the waterfront)
tags: Winter for the urchins (Jan-Mar), otherwise dinner
v07-la-sirena.why: Long-running family kitchen on a back lane; mermaid-themed dining room and a terrace, cooking the local catch to old recipes To order: Scorpionfish (escórpora) with sauce and potatoes, or garoines (sea urchins) when in season Tucked off the front on a side street — easy to walk past. Urchins are a Jan-Mar thing only.
v07-la-sirena.address: Carrer d'es Call s/n, 17488 Cadaqués, Girona
v07-la-sirena.hours: Winter for the urchins (Jan-Mar), otherwise dinner
v07-la-sirena._lane: One street back — the catch without the view

v09-es-balconet.name: Es Balconet
v09-es-balconet.neighborhood: Old town, Carrer Sant Antoni (narrow lane in the historic core)
v09-es-balconet.why: Small fishermen's-style restaurant in the old quarter — paella and the day's catch, a locals' room rather than a view table To order: Paella or the grilled catch of the day No sea view — an inland-lane room valued for cooking over scenery. Phone unverified.
v09-es-balconet._lane: One street back — the catch without the view

v11-es-trull.name: Es Trull
v11-es-trull.neighborhood: Old town, Carrer Portitxó (near the Portitxó square)
v11-es-trull.why: Long-standing old-town Catalan kitchen on Portitxó To order: Catalan grills and rice dishes; ask the day's fish Often tagged a pizza spot online, but its listing is plain Catalan cuisine — the wood-oven/pizza claim could NOT be confirmed, so order the Catalan plates.
v11-es-trull._lane: One street back — the catch without the view

v10-s-estrop.name: S'Estrop
tags: Recommended for terrace tables in summer
v10-s-estrop.why: Beachfront kitchen for fideuà, paellas and seafood with a view across the bay To order: Fideuà (the short-noodle answer to paella) with the local catch Exact street number not pinned from a primary source — address given to street level only. Phone unverified.
v10-s-estrop._lane: The beach, the hill and the cape

v12-es-bar-de-dalt.name: Es Bar de Dalt
v12-es-bar-de-dalt.neighborhood: Upper village, terrace under olive trees (above the old town)
tags: Evening, for the shade and the view down to the bay
v12-es-bar-de-dalt.why: Upper-village kitchen serving traditional cuisine on a terrace shaded by olive trees, away from the harbour crush To order: Whatever's traditional and in season — the draw is the olive-grove terrace as much as the plate Up the hill, away from the front — exact street address not pinned from a primary source. Phone unverified.
v12-es-bar-de-dalt.hours: Evening, for the shade and the view down to the bay
v12-es-bar-de-dalt._lane: The beach, the hill and the cape

v03-restaurant-cap-de-creus.name: Restaurant Cap de Creus
v03-restaurant-cap-de-creus.neighborhood: Cap de Creus headland, beside the lighthouse (~8 km / 20 min on the narrow road from Cadaqués), above Cala Culip
tags: Book ahead if driving up (a reservation lets you take a car up the single-track road); via reserves@restaurantcapdecreus.com
Lunch for the view; sunrise here is the first on the Iberian mainland
v03-restaurant-cap-de-creus.why: Opened 1991 by British biologist Christopher (Chris) Little in a former Civil Guard barracks at the easternmost point of mainland Spain — seven curries and vindaloo above a Catalan cove To order: One of the seven curries (the vindaloo) with samosas and chutney — the unlikely house specialty — or seafood rice if you want local Road is single-track and shared with buses — slow. Seasonal hours; confirm before the drive. Phone not verified — use email.
v03-restaurant-cap-de-creus.address: Carretera Cap de Creus s/n (Far de Cap de Creus), 17488 Cadaqués, Girona
v03-restaurant-cap-de-creus.hours: Lunch for the view; sunrise here is the first on the Iberian mainland
v03-restaurant-cap-de-creus.verdict: Seven curries above a Catalan cove at the edge of the mainland — the unlikely one that works.
v03-restaurant-cap-de-creus.signature: One of the seven curries (the vindaloo) with samosas and chutney.
v03-restaurant-cap-de-creus.person: Opened 1991 by British biologist Chris Little, in a former Civil Guard barracks.
v03-restaurant-cap-de-creus.caveat: Single-track road shared with buses — slow; seasonal hours, confirm first.
v03-restaurant-cap-de-creus._lane: The beach, the hill and the cape

v14-maritim-bar.name: Marítim Bar
v14-maritim-bar.neighborhood: Beachfront, Passeig Marítim (directly on the Cadaqués beach)
v14-maritim-bar.why: Opened on Sant Jaume's day (25 July) 1935; Dalí reportedly arrived by boat — arguably the best bar position on the bay To order: Cremat — the fishermen's flamed cane-rum, coffee and sugar, set alight at the table A chiringuito-style beach bar, seasonal hours; phone is a mobile and may go unanswered out of season.
v14-maritim-bar._lane: Le Bar — the rooms with a story

v13-l-hostal.name: L'Hostal
v13-l-hostal.neighborhood: Old town, on the Passeig / central waterfront square
tags: Walk-in for a drink; book if eating
v13-l-hostal.why: Founded by Italian Marci Pogany; the only bar Dalí frequented in Cadaqués — Dalí designed and signed its logo for free. Later drew Mick Jagger, García Márquez, Keith Richards, George Harrison To order: The 'Dalí eggs' tapa (a nod to the surrealist) with a drink No longer the nightclub of the Dalí era — now a drinks-and-tapas room trading on its history. Come for the legend, not a full dinner.
v13-l-hostal._lane: Le Bar — the rooms with a story

v15-cafe-tropical.name: Cafe Tropical
v15-cafe-tropical.why: A near-40-year fixture of Cadaqués nightlife; a 'bar musical' for cocktails and late dancing To order: A gin and tonic or a house cocktail; this is a late bar, not a kitchen Night spot only; exact street address not pinned from a primary source. Loud and late in summer.
v15-cafe-tropical._lane: Le Bar — the rooms with a story
